newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: FORECAST - NZ$360-75 mln profit seen for Telecom NZ.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - NZ$360-75 mln profit seen for Telecom NZ.

text.p: Telecom Corp of New Zealand Ltd is set to produce a profit of between NZ$360-375 million for the six months to June against $338.7 million the same period a year ago, analysts said on Tuesday.
They were unsure whether continued booming profits for Telecom would result in a share repurchase, as has been suggested by the company.
Either way, much would depend on the views of Bell Atlantic Corp and Ameritech Corp, who own just under half of the company.
The board will meet to discuss the issue on Thursday, the day of the result's release.
Kevin Bennett at Doyle Paterson Brown said a share repurchase appeared to be far from a done deal.
Telecom has rallied sharply to historic highs in recent weeks as speculation about a repayment resurfaced.
But Bennett said the sharp rally in the bond market may have also been a contributing factor to yield-sensitive Telecom's rally.
Analysts expect a progress report on Thursday as to what will happen with Telecom's Australian wing, Pacific Star.
The company has said it is reviewing Pacific Star, which may result in all or part of the loss-making company being sold.
The second quarter was expected to contain a loss of perhaps NZ$5-10 million from Pacific Star, plus asset writedowns associated with it.
"But I don't think the market is going to be overly concerned, provided it can see the exit strategy evolving," Bennett Said.
Sarndra Urlich at Cavill White Securities agreed the market should not be too perturbed by Pacific Star.
"I don't think Pacific Star is anything major to worry about, but it was a bad move and they will write it off for this year," she said.
If Telecom were to undertake a one-for-10 buyback at NZ$8.00 a share, the cost would be around $1.5 billion, which would significantly increase debt servicing costs.

"They can afford to do it and they can still sustain dividends and the capital expenditure programme," she said. "It just means that they will have higher gearing and more discipline imposed in terms of managing that capital."
Recent aggressive pricing initiatives by its long distance and cellular network competitors took place in the latter part of the second quarter so were only likely to be felt in the third.
More broadly, Telecom appeared to be facing a bright future.

"Generally speaking, most people have a more positive expectation for New Zealand in 1997...and the one thing about Telecom is that it is a very liquid play on the New Zealand story, which is more than you can say for some of our other leading stocks," Doyle Paterson's Bennett said.
